compoundNote: Longvida is Verdure Sciences' trademarked solid lipid curcumin particle (SLCP) formulation; a 400 mg Longvida capsule delivers roughly 80 mg curcumin (the rest is lipid/excipients and minor curcuminoids), so 'mg Longvida' and 'mg curcumin' differ by about 5x. Only studies that used Longvida by name are listed in studies[]; trials of other curcumin products (Theracurmin, BCM-95/Biocurcumax, Meriva, C3, NovaSol, plain curcumin) are not evidence for Longvida. Most Longvida trials are funded or supplied by Verdure Sciences. Two cognition trials are positive at 400 mg/day (Cox 2015, 2020); two 2 g/day trials are null for cognition (Santos-Parker 2018, CKD 2024). All pubmedUrl status values are 203 because NCBI served a bot-challenge page to curl; see statusNote.

studies.title: Investigation of the effects of solid lipid curcumin on cognition and mood in a healthy older population
studies.design: randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled; acute (1h, 3h), chronic (4 weeks) and acute-on-chronic effects (Cox, Pipingas, Scholey; epub 2014-10-02)
studies.dose: 400 mg Longvida per day (abstract says '400 mg as Longvida'; curcumin content not stated in the abstract; the same group's 2020 paper describes 400 mg Longvida as ~80 mg curcumin)
studies.outcome: Cognitive battery (sustained attention, working memory), mood, blood biomarkers incl. cholesterol and haematology
studies.result: 1h after a single dose: significantly better sustained attention and working memory vs placebo. After 4 weeks: better working memory and mood (general fatigue; calmness, contentedness and fatigue change after psychological stress). Acute-on-chronic effect on alertness and contentedness. Significantly lower total and LDL cholesterol; no effect on haematological safety measures.
studies.fundingConflict: NOT VERIFIED: paper is paywalled (SAGE); funding/COI statement not read. PubMed lists it as 'Research Support, Non-U.S. Gov't'. Same research group's 2020 follow-up was funded by Verdure Sciences.

studies.title: Further Evidence of Benefits to Mood and Working Memory from Lipidated Curcumin in Healthy Older People: A 12-Week, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled, Partial Replication Study
studies.dose: 400 mg Longvida per day containing ~80 mg curcumin (full text 2.3: 'approximately 80 mg curcumin in a SLCP formulation')
studies.form: Longvida SLCP capsule vs dextrin placebo
studies.outcome: Cognitive performance, mood (POMS, fatigue), blood/tissue biomarkers
studies.result: Better working memory at 12 weeks (Serial Threes, Serial Sevens, virtual Morris Water Maze); lower POMS fatigue at 4 and 12 weeks; lower tension, anger, confusion and total mood disturbance at 4 weeks only. Curcumin group had significantly higher fasting glucose at 12 weeks (adjusted means 5.542 vs 5.328 mmol/L, p=0.014); the authors state this was not near diabetic range. No effect on renal, liver, lipid, cytokine, CRP or oxidative-stress measures. The 2015 cholesterol reduction was not replicated.
studies.fundingConflict: Read in full text (PMC7352411, Funding and Conflicts of Interest sections): 'funded by a grant from Verdure Sciences' (Longvida's maker); authors state funders had no role in design, analysis, writing or publication decision; three authors 'have received funding from the nutrition and supplement industry'.

studies.title: Curcumin supplementation improves vascular endothelial function in healthy middle-aged and older adults by increasing nitric oxide bioavailability and reducing oxidative stress
studies.population: 39 healthy men and postmenopausal women aged 45-74
studies.dose: 2000 mg/day Longvida (~400 mg curcumin per the full text)
studies.outcome: Forearm blood-flow response to acetylcholine, brachial flow-mediated dilation, aortic pulse wave velocity, carotid compliance, oxidative stress/inflammation biomarkers
studies.result: Resistance-artery endothelial function +37% and brachial FMD +36% with curcumin vs no change on placebo; arterial stiffness and circulating oxidative-stress/inflammation biomarkers unchanged. Full text: 3 curcumin participants had expected adverse events (diarrhoea, dizziness, GI discomfort); one dizziness exclusion; no severe or unexpected adverse events.
studies.fundingConflict: Read in full text (PMC5310664): NIH awards R21 AG042795, UL1 TR001082, T32 AG000279, R37 AG013038; 'The authors have no declarations of interest'; capsules provided by Verdure Sciences.

doseAssessment.trialRange: Positive cognition/mood trials (Cox 2015, n=60; Cox 2020, n=80): 400 mg Longvida per day (~80 mg curcumin per the 2020 paper), 4 weeks (2015) and 12 weeks (2020). Null cognition trials used 2000 mg Longvida/day (~400 mg curcumin) for 12 weeks (Santos-Parker 2018, healthy adults 45-74) and 12 months (CKD patients, 2024). Other Longvida doses: 400 mg/day (DiSilvestro 2012 biomarkers; McFarlin 2016 muscle damage), 1000 mg/day (HIIT 2021), 800 mg/day (knee OA 2019).
doseAssessment.suggestedText: Positive human cognition and mood findings with Longvida come from two industry-funded trials in healthy adults aged 50-85 using 400 mg of Longvida per day (about 80 mg of curcumin) for 4 to 12 weeks. Two trials at 2,000 mg per day found no cognitive benefit.

safetySignals.signal: Cox 2020 (400 mg Longvida/day, 12 weeks): fasting blood glucose was significantly higher in the curcumin group than placebo (5.542 vs 5.328 mmol/L, p=0.014). Authors say it was not near diabetic range; relevance for people with diabetes or on glucose-lowering drugs is untested.
safetySignals.title: Further Evidence of Benefits to Mood and Working Memory from Lipidated Curcumin in Healthy Older People: A 12-Week, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled, Partial Replication Study

safetySignals.signal: CKD trial (2000 mg Longvida/day, 12 months, n=88): no serious adverse events attributed to curcumin; any adverse event 60.0% vs 48.8% placebo (NS); abdominal pain 13.3% vs 4.7% (NS); one curcumin-group COVID-19 death.
safetySignals.title: Curcumin Supplementation and Vascular and Cognitive Function in Chronic Kidney Disease: A Randomized Controlled Trial

safetySignals.signal: Knee OA pilot (800 mg Longvida/day, 90 days): one SLCP-group withdrawal due to rash and itching.
safetySignals.title: Evaluation of the efficacy and safety of Capsule Longvida® Optimized Curcumin (solid lipid curcumin particles) in knee osteoarthritis: a pilot clinical study

safetySignals.signal: General turmeric/curcumin supplement caution (not Longvida-specific): Italian phytovigilance cases and a systematic review of case reports associate Curcuma longa supplements, in these cases high-bioavailability, high-curcumin-dose products, with acute cholestatic hepatitis; positive dechallenge in most cases.
safetySignals.title: Acute liver injury following turmeric use in Tuscany: An analysis of the Italian Phytovigilance database and systematic review of case reports

safetySignals.signal: General caution (in vitro, pig liver cells, not Longvida and not a human result): curcumin inhibited CYP1A2 and CYP3A activity and the authors conclude curcumin can cause food-drug interactions with warfarin. No Longvida-specific anticoagulant study was found.
safetySignals.title: Curcumin and quercetin modify warfarin-induced regulation of porcine CYP1A2 and CYP3A expression and activity

safetySignals.signal: Preclinical safety only: Longvida was non-genotoxic in a bacterial reverse mutation test and a mouse micronucleus test (up to 2000 mg/kg/day). Not a human safety study.
safetySignals.title: Safety assessment of a solid lipid curcumin particle preparation: In vitro and in vivo genotoxicity studies

gaps: Only two small RCTs (Cox 2015 n=60; Cox 2020 n=80) show positive cognition/mood effects, both from one Melbourne research group, one confirmed funded by Verdure Sciences (the other's funding statement could not be read), both in healthy adults aged 50-85. No independent replication found.

Two Longvida trials at 2,000 mg/day were null for cognition: Santos-Parker 2018 (PMID 29951592, 12 weeks, healthy 45-74) and the CKD trial (PMID 39199229, 12 months). No Longvida RCT in MCI, dementia or Alzheimer's disease was found.
No Longvida trial tested doses between 400 and 2000 mg for cognition, nor durations beyond 12 weeks in healthy people; no dose-response data for cognition.
Cox 2015 (PMID 25277322) and the HIIT trial (PMID 34114918) full text/funding statements were not accessible (paywalled); funding for those is unverified.
No Longvida-specific data on drug interactions (warfarin, antiplatelets, diabetes drugs); the glucose finding in Cox 2020 is unreplicated.

Context only, not Longvida evidence: PMID 40487425 (iScience 2025) pharmacokinetic crossover in 9 men comparing Longvida, AOV and NovaSOL at ~570 mg; unconjugated curcumin plasma levels stayed very low for all formulations, challenging bioavailability claims.

Context only: PMID 35991218 (retinal fluorescence in Alzheimer's, 2022) gave Longvida, Theracurmin or Novasol and measured retinal imaging, not cognition; it found no AD vs control difference. Longvida plasma conjugated curcumin 198.7 nM vs 576.6 (Theracurmin) and 1605.8 (Novasol).
Context only (other formulation): PMID 30070343 tested Meriva for interaction with antiplatelets/anticoagulants (no change in bleeding time or INR); this does not transfer to Longvida.
